主要内容: On February 8, 2012, the U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) issued proposed regulations under the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA) to improve offshore tax compliance and reduce the burden on U.S. taxpayers. These regulations aim to address non-compliance by U.S. taxpayers using foreign accounts. The proposed rules outline a step-by-step process for identifying U.S. accounts, reporting information, and meeting withholding requirements for foreign financial institutions (FFIs), other foreign entities, and U.S. withholding agents. The regulations are implemented in stages to minimize administrative burdens and costs while achieving FATCA’s compliance objectives. The rules also allow time for resolving local law limitations that may affect some FFIs. The Treasury and IRS emphasized that these regulations are targeted and efficient, complementing global efforts to combat offshore tax evasion. The proposed regulations include measures to reduce administrative burdens, expand the categories of FFIs deemed compliant with FATCA, and phase in reporting and withholding obligations over an extended transition period. Additionally, the Treasury Department issued a joint statement with several European governments expressing mutual intent to pursue a government-to-government framework for implementing FATCA.
